supported_scope: Credential delivery and secure authentication via Application Default Credentials (ADC) and native OS secure keyring integration
unsupported_scope: Explicit secret redaction mechanisms in prompts or generated code
Automatic secret detection and removal from committed files
unestablished_scope: Storage and lifecycle management of secrets beyond ADC and keyring
Secret exposure boundaries within agent-generated content
Limits on secret handling and leakage prevention in prompts or code
required_setup: Enable Application Default Credentials (ADC) by setting environment variable AGY_ADC_AUTH=true or user setting enableAdc in ~/.gemini/config/config.json; sign in via local OS secure keyring or web browser for token profile acquisition
constraints: ADC usage requires explicit environment variable or user setting activation
Agent prompts for approval before executing write or terminal commands by default
Terminal sandbox can be enabled to restrict command execution and protect credentials
Non-workspace file access is off by default for safety

evidence.section: Authenticate > Sign in by surface > Application Default Credentials (ADC)
evidence.quote: Antigravity CLI ( agy ) uses secure credentials and token profiles to communicate with the shared agent harness.
evidence.claim: The CLI uses secure credentials and token profiles for communication, indicating built-in credential handling.

evidence.section: Authenticate > Sign in by surface > Application Default Credentials (ADC)
evidence.quote: Enable ADC in the CLI by setting AGY_ADC_AUTH=true (and optionally GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION )
evidence.claim: Credential delivery via ADC requires explicit environment variable activation.

evidence.section: Authenticate > Sign in by surface > Local silent keyring sign-in
evidence.quote: the CLI attempts to access your operating system’s native secure keyring (such as Apple Keychain, Linux Secret Service/dbus, or Windows Credential Manager). If a valid token profile is found, the CLI authenticates your session silently without opening a browser.
evidence.claim: The CLI supports silent authentication using native OS secure keyrings, avoiding manual credential input.

evidence.section: Settings > Antigravity CLI > Configuration options reference > Safety and permissions
evidence.quote: Tool Permission ( toolPermission ) : Controls the authorization flow for tools (such as running terminal commands): request-review (default): Prompts for your approval before running write, bash, or web tools.
evidence.claim: Agent prompts for user approval before executing potentially sensitive operations, providing control over secret exposure.
